\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نرد} (nard)}{نرد (nard)}]{\ar{نرد} (nard) — dice}

\label{lesson:AR-C539-nard}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to knit, then the Arabic for to sew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نرد}}
\textbf{\ar{نرد}} — \emph{nard} — \textquotedblleft{}dice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رمى} \ar{أخي} \ar{النرد} \ar{وفاز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ramā akhī an-nard wa-fāza.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother threw the dice and won.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نرد}} (\emph{nard}) was borrowed from Persian: it is a Persian word, arabicized, for the game of backgammon and its pieces (Lane). Today it names the dice.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nard}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nard}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ramā akhī an-nard wa-fāza.} — My brother threw the dice and won.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to knit, then the Arabic for to sew, then say \emph{nard} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نرد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Dice\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أرجوحة} (urjūḥa)}{أرجوحة (urjūḥa)}]{\ar{أرجوحة} (urjūḥa) — a swing}

\label{lesson:AR-C539-urjuha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to sew, then the Arabic for dice.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أرجوحة}}
\textbf{\ar{أرجوحة}} — \emph{urjūḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}a swing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يلعب} \ar{الأطفال} \ar{على} \ar{الأرجوحة} \ar{في} \ar{الحديقة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yalʿabu al-aṭfāl ʿalā al-urjūḥa fī al-ḥadīqa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children play on the swing in the park.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أراجيح}, \emph{arājīḥ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أرجوحة}} (\emph{urjūḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-j-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to outweigh, to go down (of a scale)\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A swing goes up and down like the pans of a scale.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{urjūḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{urjūḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yalʿabu al-aṭfāl ʿalā al-urjūḥa fī al-ḥadīqa.} — The children play on the swing in the park.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to sew, then the Arabic for dice, then say \emph{urjūḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أرجوحة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A swing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تسلى} (tasallā)}{تسلى (tasallā)}]{\ar{تسلى} (tasallā) — to have fun}

\label{lesson:AR-C539-tasalla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for dice, then the Arabic for a swing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تسلى}}
\textbf{\ar{تسلى}} — \emph{tasallā} — \textquotedblleft{}to have fun\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تسلينا} \ar{بلعب} \ar{الورق} \ar{في} \ar{المساء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tasallaynā bi-laʿib al-waraq fī al-masāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We had fun playing cards in the evening.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتسلى}, \emph{yatasallā}.

\ar{لعب} \ar{الورق} is playing cards.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تسلى}} (\emph{tasallā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-l-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to forget, to be consoled\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form V tasallā is to take one's mind off things.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasallā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasallā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasallaynā bi-laʿib al-waraq fī al-masāʾ.} — We had fun playing cards in the evening.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for dice, then the Arabic for a swing, then say \emph{tasallā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تسلى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To have fun\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بستنة} (bastana)}{بستنة (bastana)}]{\ar{بستنة} (bastana) — gardening}

\label{lesson:AR-C539-bastana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a swing, then the Arabic for to have fun.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بستنة}}
\textbf{\ar{بستنة}} — \emph{bastana} — \textquotedblleft{}gardening\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يقضي} \ar{جدي} \ar{وقته} \ar{في} \ar{البستنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaqḍī jaddī waqtahu fī al-bastana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather spends his time gardening.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بستنة}} (\emph{bastana}) is a modern Arabic noun built from \emph{bustān}, \textquotedblleft{}an orchard\textquotedblright{}, which you know: Arabic made a four-letter root \emph{b-s-t-n} from it. \emph{Bustān} is usually traced to Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bastana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bastana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaqḍī jaddī waqtahu fī al-bastana.} — My grandfather spends his time gardening.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a swing, then the Arabic for to have fun, then say \emph{bastana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بستنة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Gardening\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تأرجح} (taʾarjaḥa)}{تأرجح (taʾarjaḥa)}]{\ar{تأرجح} (taʾarjaḥa) — to swing}

\label{lesson:AR-C539-taarjaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to have fun, then the Arabic for gardening.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تأرجح}}
\textbf{\ar{تأرجح}} — \emph{taʾarjaḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}to swing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تأرجحت} \ar{البنت} \ar{على} \ar{الأرجوحة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʾarjaḥat al-bint ʿalā al-urjūḥa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The girl swung on the swing.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتأرجح}, \emph{yataʾarjaḥ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تأرجح}} (\emph{taʾarjaḥa}) goes with \emph{urjūḥa}, \textquotedblleft{}a swing\textquotedblright{}, built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-j-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to outweigh, to go down (of a scale pan)\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾarjaḥat al-bint ʿalā al-urjūḥa.} — The girl swung on the swing.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to have fun, then the Arabic for gardening, then say \emph{taʾarjaḥa} again
\end{itemize}
